title: Decimal place value & ordering
examples: How do I know if zero matters when I am comparing decimals?
Can you show me how to compare decimals that have different numbers of digits?
What is the rule for adding or comparing decimals with lots of zeros?

explain.say: Today we are learning to compare decimals correctly. We will look at place value first.
Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: base-ten blocks. Look at the thousand, the hundreds and the tens. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
When comparing decimals, you must always start from the largest place value. Look at the ones place first.
If the digits in the ones place are the same, move to the next place value to the right. This is the tenths place.

items: Tenths place: If same, move right
Next place: Keep moving until difference

explain.say: If the tenths are the same, you keep moving right until you find a difference. Remember to count all the places.
A zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value. For example, zero point five is the same as zero point five zero.

items: Zero at the end doesn't change value

faq.q: When should I worry about the number of digits?
faq.a: You should not worry about the number of digits. You can add zeros to the end to make them match. This helps you compare them easily.
asks: Do I need to make them the same length?
Does it matter if one has fewer digits?

faq.q: Is zero always important in decimals?
faq.a: No, a zero at the end does not change the value. For example, five point two is the same as five point two zero.

faq.q: If the first two digits are the same, what do I do next?
faq.a: If the first two digits are the same, you must move to the next place value. You keep comparing digits until you find a difference.
asks: Where do I look after the tenths place?
What if the first three digits match?

faq.q: How do I compare zero point five and zero point four five?
faq.a: You can write zero point five as zero point five zero. Then you compare the digits place by place. Five tenths is bigger than four tenths.
asks: How do I compare these two numbers?

faq.q: Does the zero in the middle matter?
faq.a: Yes, a zero in a place value position matters. For example, zero point one five is different from zero point five one.
asks: Why is the zero important here?

facts: When comparing decimals, always start comparing from the largest place value.
A zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value.
You can add zeros to the end of a decimal to match the number of places.
Zero point five is mathematically equal to zero point five zero.

quiz.say: Which is larger: zero point seven or zero point six nine?
quiz.why: When you compare them, seven tenths is larger than six tenths, so zero point seven is bigger.

wrong.0: This mistake happens because you think there is no single mathematical rule for comparison.
wrong.2: This mistake happens because you only look at the first digit and stop there.
wrong.3: This mistake happens because you forget to add the zero to make them match in length.

quiz.say: Order these from smallest to largest: zero point three, zero point three zero, zero point zero three.

options.show: zero point zero three, zero point three zero, zero point three
options.say: zero point zero three, zero point three zero, zero point three

options.show: zero point three, zero point three zero, zero point zero three
options.say: zero point three, zero point three zero, zero point zero three

options.show: zero point three zero, zero point three, zero point zero three
options.say: zero point three zero, zero point three, zero point zero three

options.show: zero point zero three, zero point three, zero point three zero
options.say: zero point zero three, zero point three, zero point three zero

quiz.why: You must compare the tenths place first. Zero point zero three has zero in the tenths place, which is the smallest.

wrong.0: This mistake happens because you incorrectly assume that more digits always mean a larger number.
wrong.1: This mistake happens because you are treating the trailing zero as making the number bigger.
wrong.2: This mistake happens because you are comparing the numbers as if they were whole numbers.

quiz.say: Which number is the same value as zero point four five?
quiz.why: Adding a zero at the end does not change the actual value of the decimal number.

wrong.0: This mistake happens because you are removing a place value that actually exists.
wrong.1: This mistake happens because you are changing the digit in the hundredths place.
wrong.2: This mistake happens because you are forgetting the decimal point entirely.
